newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul finance minister opposes quick-fix measures.
newsitem.headline: Seoul finance minister opposes quick-fix measures.

text.p: South Korea's new Finance Minister said on Thursday he would not take quick-fix steps to boost the sagging economy which could trigger side-effects.
"Artificial boosting measures will be avoided as much as possible," said Kang Kyung-shik.
Kang also told reporters he would review ways of improving the real-name system, which bans the use of first names in financial transactions.
He said it was important to strengthen competitiveness by reviving the market mechanism and cutting through red tape.
"Among others, over-consumption is a big headache at the moment," he said.

President Kim Young-sam appointed Kang as new Finance and Economy Minister on Wednesday in a sweeping cabinet reshuffle aimed at restoring his presidency, which has been tarnished by the Hanbo scandal.
Kang said that the current real-name system caused bottlenecks in the economy and needed changes.
"I think it is necessary to fix the tax system as it relates to real-name financial transactions," Kang said.
He was an early advocate of the real-name financial system in the early 1980s when he was finance minister under former former president Chun Doo Hwan.
